title: VOID Workshop: open-source, approval-first AI coding agent for Linux, with the VOID Portal phone remote
description: VOID Workshop is a free, open-source desktop coding agent for Linux built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use your Claude plan, an API key or local Ollama models; review a diff before every write and approve every command. VOID Portal lets you drive it from your Android phone, end-to-end encrypted.
keywords: AI coding agent, Claude Agent SDK, Claude Code alternative, Linux desktop app, local AI coding, Ollama, code review, approval, Android remote, Tauri
ogTitle: VOID Workshop: your code, your key, your approval
ogDescription: Open-source, approval-first AI coding workspace for Linux, plus VOID Portal, an end-to-end encrypted Android remote. By M4S4T0-V01D.
ldWorkshop: Local, approval-first AI coding workspace for Linux built on the Claude Agent SDK, with diffs before every write, approvals before every command, and spending limits.

heroTitle:
Your code. Your key.
Your approval.
heroLead: VOID Workshop is a free, open-source desktop coding agent for Linux built on the Claude Agent SDK. It plans before it touches anything, shows a diff before every write, asks before every command, and stops at the budget you set. Bring your Claude plan, an API key or local Ollama models, and drive it from your phone with VOID Portal.
shotAlt: The VOID Workshop window: file tree, agent conversation, plan and changes panels, terminal and status bar
howSub: Describe what you want in plain English. The agent does the legwork; you stay in charge of every change.
flow1d: The agent can only see that folder, plus directories you explicitly add.
flow2d: Plain English. Follow-ups continue the same session.
flow3d: Read-only exploration first. Nothing is edited until you approve.
flow4d: A diff for every write; command, folder and reason for every command.
flow5d: Accept or reject each file, run tests, commit when you choose.
reviewSub: Every edit arrives as a unified diff before it's written. If the file changes on disk while you're deciding, the edit is refused, so your own work is never silently overwritten.
review1: Proposed → applied → tested → committed: clear states for every file.
review2: Per-file accept / reject restores the original content on reject.
review3: Local Git checkpoints that never touch your branch or index.
review4: Commits only when you click Commit. Never a push.
reviewAlt: Approval dialog showing a unified diff for a proposed file change
safetyTitle: Built like the model is untrusted
safetySub: Model output and repository content are treated as untrusted input. Approval is the first layer, not the only one.
safe1d: Exact command, working directory, the agent's reason and what the command does (reads, writes, network, git, installs). Approvals are never remembered.
safe2d: Agent commands can only write inside the project and can't reach the network unless you allow specific domains.
safe3d: sudo, broad rm -rf, pushes, history rewrites, publishing, uploads, SSH, keyring access and attempts to touch the app's own config are refused outright.
safe4d: .., symlinks and ~ can't escape the project. SSH keys, cloud credentials, browser profiles and keyrings are always off limits.
safe5d: .env, private keys and credential files need explicit approval. Logs, history and the UI are redacted.
safe6d: Refuses to run as root. No author server, proxy or analytics: the only destinations are the model provider you chose and, for VOID Portal, the relay you deployed yourself.
billTitle: Your plan or your key. Honest numbers.
billSub: Use your Claude plan or an Anthropic Console API key stored in your desktop keyring, and switch with one click. VOID Workshop checks the credential source before sending a single request.
bill1: Per-task and daily limits (defaults: $1 and $3), plus turn and output-token caps.
bill2: Stops on credit exhaustion and never buys credits or switches billing.
bill3: Models come from the Models API for your key; none are hard-coded.
bill4: Pair it with a Console workspace spend limit for a hard cap.
billNote: Estimates, not a balance. Cost figures are estimated from the token usage the Agent SDK reports. Retries, caching, price changes and other usage in your organization all affect the real bill, and there's no API for an app to read your remaining credit. VOID Workshop says so in the status bar and links you to Console Billing.
editorAlt: The built-in code editor in the Nebula theme, syntax colours derived from the theme
editorTitle: A real editor, in your colours
editorSub: Open any project file in the built-in CodeMirror editor, make a quick fix yourself, and hand the rest to the agent. Syntax highlighting is generated from your theme, so every theme, including the ones you make, gets matching colours.
editor1: Tabs, search and save, and a warning when the agent or another program changed the file on disk.
editor2: Multiple cursors, and undo history kept across project switches.
editor3: Sensitive files ask first before they open or save.
portalTitle: VOID Portal: your phone as a remote
portalSub: The Android companion app. Start and queue tasks from anywhere, approve changes and commands (straight from the notification if you like), switch model, mode and account, and hear when a task is done, needs you, or the PC goes offline.
wire:
phone ──wss──► your relay ◄──wss── PC
└──── end-to-end encrypted, AES-256-GCM ────┘
portal1: Pair with a QR code. The secret lives only in the code; the relay never sees it, your prompts or your code.
portal2: Nothing exposed at home. Both ends connect out, so there are no open ports or port forwarding.
portal3: Same rules as the desktop. Blocked commands stay blocked; risky ones still need your approval.
portal4: Themes that match your PC, Material You, and a recoloured app icon.
portalAlt1: VOID Portal home screen: PC online, active tasks and a pending approval
portalCap1: PC status, tasks, what needs you
portalAlt2: Approving a file change with its diff on the phone
portalAlt3: A task conversation in VOID Portal
portalCap3: Follow and reply to a task
portalAlt4: VOID Portal settings and theme picker
relayTitle: Run your own relay in five minutes
relaySub: There is no shared relay: everyone deploys their own on a free Cloudflare account, so your traffic never passes through anyone else's server. The free Workers tier is plenty for one person.
relay1d: Sign up free and pick a workers.dev subdomain.
relay3d: The smoke test runs 18 checks against your relay.
relay5d: Pair a phone, then scan the QR code in the app.
relayC1: from your clone of the repository
relayC2: authorise wrangler in the browser, once
relayC3: optional: in-app updates for VOID Portal (or delete the [[r2_buckets]] block in wrangler.toml)
relayAfter: Then enter wss://void-relay.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev in Settings → VOID Portal (phone) → Relay. Lost a pairing code or a phone? Unpair the device in the same place and its key stops working. The full guide is in remote/README.md.
themesSub: Seven built-in themes, a live colour editor with contrast warnings, and JSON import/export so you can share themes.
themesTry: Click a theme to try it on this page.
themesAlt: Theme editor in the settings dialog
installSub: Builds from source in a few minutes and installs for your user only. No root, no system files.
inst1b: Debian / Ubuntu 24.04+ (plus Node.js 22 and Rust from nodejs.org / rustup.rs)
inst3: 3. launch, then Settings → Sign-in & API key: sign in with Claude, paste a key, or pick Ollama
instPortal: cd remote/android && ./gradlew :app:assembleRelease (JDK 17), install the APK on your phone, then pair it with your relay
instUninstallD: ./scripts/uninstall.sh (add --purge to delete history, settings and the stored key)
faqSub: The short answers. The guides in the repository have the long ones.
a1: VOID Workshop and VOID Portal are free and open source (MIT). You pay only for the model you use: your Claude plan, Anthropic API usage on your own Console account, or nothing with local Ollama models. The relay fits in Cloudflare's free tier.
q2: Does my code or my key go anywhere?
a2: Only to the model provider you chose. There is no telemetry and no author server. Keys stay in your desktop keyring, and VOID Portal traffic is end-to-end encrypted through the relay you deploy yourself.
q3: How is it different from Claude Code?
a3: It runs the same Claude Agent SDK in a desktop window built around review: a diff before every write, an approval for every command, per-file accept and reject, a sandbox, spending limits, and a phone remote.
q4: Which systems does it run on?
a4: Linux (developed on Arch, works on Debian/Ubuntu and others with WebKitGTK 4.1). VOID Portal needs Android 8 or newer.
q5: Can I use someone else's relay?
a5: Don't: deploy your own. It takes a few minutes, it's free, and it keeps your traffic and availability in your hands.
